Lessons.Title: Relate Fractions to Benchmarks
ExplanationParagraphs: Original First Edition2021 Grade4 Unit2 Lesson6 — Relate Fractions to Benchmarks. Read original teacher preparation, teacher lesson, and 5-page student task PDF. The existing Edulytics grade4 goal, fraction benchmark explanations and correctly authored comparison examples are preserved.

Warm-up Notice and Wonder (10min): the first number-line image contains an unlabelled point but insufficient numerical reference. Reason why knowing one benchmark alone may tell direction but cannot uniquely determine the point. Teacher moderates source image.

Activity1 Greater Than or Less Than1 (20min): original student p2 has FOUR point diagrams. For every one, identify its fraction, compare with1 and find the exact distance from1: 9/10 is below1 by1/10; 6/5 is above by1/5; 9/8 above by1/8;5/4 above by1/4. The unit is fixed; evaluate the original tick intervals. Teacher reviews full line drawings.

Activity2 Card Sort Where Do They Belong (OPTIONAL 20min), original student p3: cards from a teacher-only blackline master sorted below, equal or above one-half. Peer group checks category choices and completes the source sentence starters. Original blackline deck not present as learner task PDF; teacher supplies it. Edulytics does not claim exact publisher-card parity.

Activity3 Greater Than or Less Than1/2 (15min): original student p4 four line points:1/3 (=2/6) below half by1/6;1 greater by1/2;3/8 below by1/8;2/5 below by1/10. To locate half on original last fifths-based line, subdivide every fifth into tenths, then mark5/10. Exact distances are interpretive numerical subskills; drawing and explanation remain teacher-assessed.
Lesson synthesis (10min): compare relative to0, half and1 and interpret positive differences as distances from a benchmark. Fraction-subtraction algorithms are not the target of this source lesson.

Independent first-party Edulytics five-minute Cool-down (NOT original educator-restricted publisher task): on a fifths number line show2/5 and1/2; divide fifths into tenths and explain2/5 is1/10 below1/2. Teacher checks drawing; existing fraction benchmark question family covers a supplementary exact numeric check.

KeyConcepts.Title: Benchmark half
KeyConcepts.Definition: Halfway between0 and1 of the same whole.
KeyConcepts.Rule: n/d compared to1/2 is determined by comparing2n with d.

KeyConcepts.Title: Benchmark one
KeyConcepts.Definition: One whole at the unit location on a consistently scaled number line.
KeyConcepts.Rule: n/d is below/equal/above1 when n is below/equal/above d.

KeyConcepts.Title: Distance without subtraction algorithm
KeyConcepts.Definition: How much number-line length separates a point and a benchmark.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Use subdivisions, equivalent fractions and count unit steps.

WorkedExamples.Title: One benchmark example
WorkedExamples.Question: Where is 6/5 relative to1?
Steps: 6/5 lies one equal fifth to the right of5/5.

WorkedExamples.Title: Odd denominator, benchmark half
WorkedExamples.Question: How far is2/5 from half?
WorkedExamples.Method: Subdivide each fifth into two tenths.
WorkedExamples.Check: Original source last line uses fifths before subdivision.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Naming a point from a single unlabeled interval with no unit reference.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Original warm-up requires enough numeric information to know the scale.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Find two reference positions and equal spacing.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Confusing fraction-size comparison with the distance to the benchmark.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The source asks for both comparison and exact distance.
CommonMistakes.Correction: State value, relation and step-sized gap.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Forcing1/2 onto an unsplit fifths tick.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Half falls between two fifths ticks.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Partition fifths into tenths and mark5/10.

SummaryPoints: 2021 student PDF5p: warm-up, four point tasks compared with1, optional card sort around half, four point tasks compared with half, section summary.
Four source greater/less-than1 line values and exact distances are recorded as a teacher reference.
Original optional blackline card list not present in source student PDF; teacher checks activity, no invented source card identities.
At half, three originals use existing unit ticks; last subdivides fifths into tenths.
Original .NET and authenticated UI StageD test not run; existing exact benchmark family is supplementary only.
